info.text:
Buy now, pay later is sold as zero interest, so how do lenders make billions? This video follows a $400 pay-in-four order to show the merchant fee stores pay (our math uses the CFPB's 2.49% average from 2021), then shows why Affirm earned about 48% of its fiscal 2026 revenue from interest, how Klarna's mix differs, and what late fees really add. We also cover late payments and overdrafts in the Fed's 2025 survey, credit reporting and FICO's BNPL scores, and how the CFPB's 2024 rule was withdrawn in 2025.

Sources: Affirm Form 10-K, fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, and fiscal Q1 2027 results (Nov 5, 2026); Affirm S-1 (2020) and 10-Ks (GMV history); Klarna full-year 2025 results (Feb 26, 2026) and Q2 2026 results (Aug 2026); Klarna IPO coverage, American Banker (Sept 2025); CFPB, Buy Now, Pay Later: Market Trends and Consumer Impacts (Sept 2022) and BNPL market report (Dec 2025); Congressional Research Service, R48858 (Feb 18, 2026); Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 (May 2026); Richmond Fed Economic Brief 25-03 (2025); Protect Borrowers BNPL report (2026); Affirm/Experian credit reporting release (March 2025); LendingTree BNPL survey (March 2026); FICO (June 23, 2025); Federal Register 90 FR 20084 (May 12, 2025).

News and education, not financial advice.

#buynowpaylater #personalfinance #economics
